stem: Why is the spin-only formula generally unsuitable for predicting the magnetic moments of lanthanide ions?
options: Lanthanide ions have no unpaired electrons
The $4f$ electrons have no spin angular momentum
The $4f$ subshell is always completely filled
The orbital angular momentum of the $4f$ electrons is not fully quenched

verdicts.working: In lanthanide ions, the 4f electrons’ orbital angular momentum is not fully quenched, so it contributes to the magnetic moment alongside spin.

working:
Lanthanide $4f$ electrons retain a significant orbital contribution; their magnetic moments depend on both spin and orbital angular momentum.

Independent check: In lanthanide ions, the 4f electrons’ orbital angular momentum is not fully quenched, so it contributes to the magnetic moment alongside spin.
solution: The spin-only formula neglects orbital angular momentum. In lanthanide ions, the $4f$ electrons’ orbital contribution is not fully quenched, so the magnetic moment depends on both spin and orbital angular momentum.
